newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Aziz to seek Russia's help on sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz to seek Russia's help on sanctions.

text.p: Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz will leave for Moscow on Monday to seek Russia's help in having curbs on Iraqi oil exports lifted, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

INA, quoting Aziz, said the visit, the second in three months, would focus on U.N. disarmament activities. Under the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire terms the ban on Iraqi oil exports can only be lifted if the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) testifies that Baghdad has come clean on all its disarmament obligations.
"During my previous visit I conducted talks with (Russian Foreign Minister) Yevgeni Primakov on the the subject of the embargo imposed on Iraq and steps needed to have it removed," Aziz told INA.
He said he also told Russian leaders that UNSCOM, charged with the scrapping of Iraq's weapons of mass destruction, was resorting to tactics to delay the end of its work in Iraq.
"My visit this time comes within the same framework," he said.
He said Russia had a sound attitude on matters related to Iraq, calling for a swift lifting of sanctions. "We appreciate such a stand," he said.
Aziz accused UNSCOM chairman Rolf Ekeus of adopting anti- Iraq attitudes and giving conflicting statements on his disarmament work in Iraq
"When he is in Iraq he says something which is nearly positive and objective ... when he goes to Kuwait he says something to please the Kuwaiti regime," he said.
"In my appreciation such deviating attitudes by Ekeus have become more known than before," Aziz said.
Aziz said he raised the issue with Ekeus several times and urged him to be more careful in his press statements in future.
Aziz reiterated Iraq had no more banned weapons left in its arsenal. Ekeus says Baghdad still needs to verify that it got rid of these weapons.
Ekeus was in Baghdad last month and gained Iraqi approval to have wrecked missile parts taken outside for examination.
Diplomats in Baghdad said the visit to Russia by Aziz was part of a fresh diplomatic offensive by Baghdad to lobby for the lifting of sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf is in New York holding talks with U.N. officials on Iraq's oil-for-food deal with U.N. allowing Baghdad oil exports worth $2 billion in six months for humanitarian purposes.
Iraq on Sunday accused the United States of attempting to impede the arrival of food and medicine under the deal.
"In the (U.N.) Security Council there are several countries such as America and Britain adopting a ... hostile attitude vis-a-vis Iraq," Aziz said.
